propositions: Amending a commit with `git commit --amend -F <file>` or `-m` drops the Change-Id trailer, causing Gerrit to stamp a new one and create a duplicate change instead of a new patchset.
Hooks (prepare-commit-msg and Gerrit's commit-msg) cannot detect and prevent this because git does not indicate to the hook that `-F` is part of an amend operation.
A `make amend-msg FILE=<path>` wrapper must extract the existing Change-Id from HEAD, amend with the new message content, and restore the original Change-Id to prevent duplicate changes.
The wrapper must fail loudly and refuse to amend if HEAD carries no Change-Id, indicating a missing pre-commit hook installation.
AGENTS.md documentation must be updated to name `make amend-msg` as the standard path for rewriting commit messages and explicitly warn that `--amend -m/-F` create duplicate Gerrit changes.
